# Aleph v0.1

Aleph is a programming language whose primary authors and readers are AI agents. Goals: few tokens, native speed, correctness on the first attempt, safe by default. Human readability is NOT a goal of the source text; humans read the generated explanation (`aleph explain`).

## 1. Source files
`.aph`; UTF-8; outside strings only printable ASCII and LF. LF only; no tabs, trailing spaces or empty lines; exactly one final LF. One file = one module (imports v0.2).

## 2. Lexical structure
One space between tokens. Column 0 = item; one leading space = `fn` body line. ident `[a-z][a-z0-9]*`; int `0|-?[1-9][0-9]*`; float `-?[0-9]+\.[0-9]+`; string `"..."` escapes `\n \t \" \\`; `@f` fnref; `.f` field; `x:` param; `[1 2]`; ops `+ - * / % == != < <= > >=`. Keywords: `fn type use let do ex doc if try some none ok err else has isok empty nil true false and or not neg`.

## 3. Top-level items and canonical order
Order: `use` sorted by full canonical line text, `type` by name, `fn` by name (`main` last). Body: <=1 `doc`, then `ex E = E`+ (E001; unless `main`/effectful), then `let`/`do`*, then one result `E`. Items: `use CAP ["PREFIX"]`; `type NAME FIELD*` (field `f:T`; ctor `NAME a b`; access `.f e`); `fn NAME PARAM* -> TYPE` (param `x:T`; `main` no params -> `unit` or `res unit str`). Item `fn`/`type` names are unique, not builtin/type names (P001).

## 4. Types
`i64 f64 bool str unit`; `list T`; `opt T`; `res T E`; record. Prefix, fixed arity. Static bidirectional checking; signatures explicit, `let` inferred; no conversions/subtyping/overloading; builtins may be generic. v0.2: `dict`, JSON, sums, generics.

## 5. Expressions
Prefix, fixed arity, no parentheses; call arity from signatures, constructors and builtins. `+ - * / %` 2 same numeric (`%` i64); `== !=` 2 same primitive -> bool; `< <= > >=` 2 numeric -> bool; `and or` 2 bool short-circuit; `not` 1 bool; `neg` 1 numeric; `if c a b` 3 bool/same; `[e..]` n>=1 list T; `empty T`/`none T` 1 type; `.f e` 1 field; `some`/`ok`/`err` 1; `try e` 1 res T E -> T or early err (fn returns `res U E`); `else e d` 2 opt/res default T; `has e`/`isok e` 1 -> bool. `@f` is a function value, only as a higher-order argument.

### 5.1 Builtins (v0.1)
`e`: p pure, E effectful; `cap`: - none or capability name.

|name|signature|e|cap|
|---|---|---|---|
|args|()->list str|p|-|
|at|list T,i64->opt T|p|-|
|cat|str,str->str|p|-|
|contains|str,str->bool|p|-|
|count|str->i64|p|-|
|eprint|str->unit|E|-|
|filter|(A->bool),list A->list A|p|-|
|float|str->res f64 str|p|-|
|fold|(B,A->B),B,list A->B|p|-|
|int|str->res i64 str|p|-|
|join|list str,str->str|p|-|
|len|list T->i64|p|-|
|lower|str->str|p|-|
|map|(A->B),list A->list B|p|-|
|print|str->unit|E|-|
|push|list T,T->list T|p|-|
|range|i64,i64->list i64|p|-|
|read|str->res str str|E|fs.read|
|rev|list T->list T|p|-|
|show|T->str (T primitive or list of primitive)|p|-|
|slice|list T,i64,i64->list T|p|-|
|sort|list T->list T (T primitive)|p|-|
|split|str,str->list str|p|-|
|sum|list i64->i64|p|-|
|trim|str->str|p|-|
|upper|str->str|p|-|
|write|str,str->res unit str|E|fs.write|

## 8. Capabilities (ADR-0008)
Deny by default. `use fs.read "PREFIX"` / `use fs.write "PREFIX"`. `net.host`/`env`/`time` parse in v0.1 but have no builtins until v0.2. Relative/absolute POSIX prefixes, normalized (empty/`.` dropped), `..` never covered. Empty prefix, `..`, or a filesystem capability without a path -> C003. Literals checked statically (C001/C002); computed paths at run time (R003). stdout/stderr allowed. Traps (JSON stderr, exit 70): R001 overflow, R002 division by zero, R003 capability, R004 stack, R005 allocation.

## Semantics
T005: params/lets may not reuse a param/local/fn/ctor/builtin name. `ex` sides see globals only; examples run hermetically (fs denied -> R003, empty args, discarded output). `print`/`eprint` add one LF (stderr flushes stdout). `show`: i64 decimal; f64 Rust `{:?}` (`1.0`, `0.1`, `1e20`); list `[1 2]` (str elements quoted, `[]` empty); top-level str raw. `upper`/`lower` ASCII only. `at` negative/oob -> `none`; `slice` clamps to `[0 len]`; `range a b` half-open (`a>=b` empty, >10,000,000 elements -> R005); `sort` ascending; `count` bytes; `split s ""` -> Unicode chars (`split "" ""` -> `[]`); `int` `-?[0-9]+` in i64 (leading zeros) else `err "invalid int"`; `float` `-?[0-9]+\.[0-9]+` else `err "invalid float"`. `ok`/`err` need an expected `res` type else T010. recursion >10,000 calls or deep evaluation -> R004. `main` `err e` -> stderr, exit 1.

## 9. Diagnostics (ADR-0011)
JSON lines: required `code severity file line col msg`; optional `node expected found fix canonical`; lowercase msg; `fix` (replace/insert) only when certain. Prefixes: L lex, P parse, F format, T type, C cap, E example, R runtime, X tool. Codes: L001-L002 P001-P003 F001 T001-T008 T010 E001-E002 C001-C003 R001-R005 X001-X011.

## 10. Canonical form (ADR-0003)
AST is truth; text is its canonical printing. `aleph fmt` prints it; `aleph check` rejects different text (F001) with `canonical`. Invariant: `print(parse(t)) == t`; `parse(print(ast)) == ast`.

## 11. Command line (`aleph`)
`llms` prints this text; `check FILE [--json]`; `fmt FILE [-w]`; `test FILE [--json]`; `run FILE [ARGS..]`; `build FILE -o OUT`; `explain FILE [--json]`; `ast FILE`; `tokens FILE` (v0.2). Exit 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage, 70 trap.

## Examples
Canonical, check-clean programs (verbatim from `tests/aph/`):

```
fn demo -> unit
 ex sort [3 1 2] = [1 2 3]
 ex else at [10 20] 1 0 = 20
 ex at [10] 2 = none i64
 ex slice [1 2 3 4] 1 3 = [2 3]
 ex push [1 2] 3 = [1 2 3]
 ex rev [1 2 3] = [3 2 1]
 ex sum [1 2 3] = 6
 ex float "1.5" = ok 1.5
 ex else float "x" 0.0 = 0.0
 ex and true false = false
 ex or false true = true
 ex not false = true
 ex neg 5 = -5
 ex == 2 2 = true
 ex != 2 3 = true
 nil
fn main -> unit
 print show sort [3 1 2]
```

```
fn main -> unit
 do print cat "a" "b"
 do print show count "abc"
 do print show split "a,b,c" ","
 do print join ["a" "b"] "-"
 do print trim "  hi  "
 do print upper "aBc"
 do print lower "aBc"
 do print show contains "abc" "b"
 nil
```

```
use fs.read "data"
use fs.write "out"
fn up text:str -> str
 ex up "aB c" = "AB C"
 upper text
fn main -> res unit str
 let text try read "data/in.txt"
 let saved try write "out/up.txt" up text
 ok nil
```

```
fn pick o:opt i64 -> i64
 ex pick some 5 = 5
 ex pick none i64 = 0
 else o 0
fn plus r:res i64 str -> res i64 str
 ex plus ok 41 = ok 42
 ex plus err "x" = err "x"
 let n try r
 ok + n 1
fn main -> res unit str
 do print show pick some 5
 do print show pick none i64
 do print show else ok 7 0
 do print show else err "x" 9
 do print show has some 1
 do print show isok plus ok 41
 do print show isok plus err "x"
 let n try plus ok 41
 do print show n
 ok nil
```

```
fn add a:i64 b:i64 -> i64
 ex add 2 3 = 5
 + a b
fn inc n:i64 -> i64
 ex inc 1 = 2
 + n 1
fn positive n:i64 -> bool
 ex positive 1 = true
 > n 0
fn main -> unit
 do print show map @inc [1 2 3]
 do print show filter @positive [-1 0 2]
 do print show fold @add 0 [1 2 3 4]
 nil
```

```
type point x:i64 y:i64
fn shift p:point d:i64 -> point
 ex shift point 1 2 10 = point 11 2
 point + .x p d .y p
fn main -> unit
 let p shift point 1 2 10
 do print show .x p
 do print show .y p
 nil
```

```
fn fib n:i64 -> i64
 ex fib 0 = 0
 ex fib 1 = 1
 ex fib 10 = 55
 if < n 2 n + fib - n 1 fib - n 2
fn main -> unit
 print show fib 30
```

```
fn main -> unit
 do print "out1"
 do eprint "err1"
 do print "out2"
 do eprint "err2"
 nil
```

```
fn main -> unit
 print show len args
```

```
fn main -> unit
 do print show [1 2 3]
 do print show [1.0 2.5]
 do print show ["a b" "c"]
 do print show empty i64
 do print show 1.0
 nil
```
